holidays.name: National Bourbon Day
holidays.description: A day to raise a glass of America's native spirit, whether you sip it neat, on the rocks, or shaken into an Old Fashioned. Distilleries and bars across the country offer tastings and specials.
holidays.origin: Bourbon was declared a 'distinctive product of the United States' by Congress in 1964. The unofficial day of celebration grew out of that tradition and is observed in mid-June by bourbon fans and distillers.
holidays.funFact: To be legally called bourbon, the spirit must be made from at least 51 percent corn and aged in new, charred oak barrels, which is why no two barrels are ever used twice for bourbon.

holidays.name: Flag Day
holidays.description: A patriotic day when Americans fly the Stars and Stripes and remember the adoption of the national flag. Parades, flag ceremonies, and backyard banners are common.
holidays.origin: The Continental Congress adopted the design of the American flag on June 14, 1777. President Woodrow Wilson officially established Flag Day in 1916, and Congress made it a national observance in 1949.
holidays.funFact: Flag Day is not a federal holiday, though Pennsylvania is the only state that observes it as a state holiday.

holidays.name: World Blood Donor Day
holidays.description: A global day to thank voluntary blood donors and encourage more people to roll up their sleeves and give the gift of life. Cookies and juice are, of course, mandatory.
holidays.origin: The World Health Organization established it in 2004. June 14 was chosen to honor the birthday of Karl Landsteiner, who discovered the ABO blood group system.
holidays.funFact: Karl Landsteiner won the Nobel Prize in 1930 for his blood group discovery, which made safe transfusions possible.

holidays.name: Pop Goes the Weasel Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the quirky nursery rhyme and its catchy jack-in-the-box tune. Participants hum, sing, and spring open boxes with gleeful surprise.
holidays.origin: The song dates to 18th-century England and became a popular dance tune in the 1850s. The date is an informal observance created by fans of oddball folk tunes.
holidays.funFact: Nobody is entirely sure what 'pop goes the weasel' means. Theories include pawning a coat (a 'weasel') or a hat-making tool.

holidays.name: Strawberry Shortcake Day
holidays.description: A sweet celebration of the classic dessert of fresh strawberries, whipped cream, and tender biscuit or sponge cake, perfect for early summer.
holidays.origin: Strawberry shortcake has American roots going back to the 1800s, when strawberry festivals and biscuit-based desserts were popular. Food-day enthusiasts mark mid-June, when strawberries peak, for its celebration.
holidays.funFact: The original American shortcake was more like a biscuit than a sponge cake, and 'short' refers to the crumbly texture created by butter.
